(Studio: Brian Williams) Report introduced. 
 (Washington: Andrea Mitchell) The controversy over President Bush’s nomination of Representative Porter Goss† to be the new CIA director featured; details given of Goss’ background, of criticism of Goss’ political views and of uncertainty over how a new CIA director will fit into Bush’s decision to create a national intelligence director. [BUSH – says he’s the right man to lead this agency.] [June 23, GOSS – comments on the getting the best possible intelligence to decision-makers.] [Senator Pat ROBERTS†- supports Goss.] [Former CIA director Stansfield TURNER††- opposes the appointment.] [June 23, Representative Jane HARMAN†- criticizes Goss for distorting the record.] [Senator Richard DURBIN†- says we’re in a total state of confusion.]

data.segment_title: Iraq / Prison Abuse Scandal / Al-Sadr Revolt
data.segment_description:
(Studio: Brian Williams) Report introduced. 
 (Pentagon: Jim Miklaszewski) A military investigation claiming that responsibility in the Iraq prison abuse scandal may reach to top commanders, possibly including Gen. Ricardo Sanchez, featured; details given of recommendations by Maj. Gen. George Fay† that may include criminal charges against military intelligence officers; courtroom sketches by Pat Lopez shown of the hearing for Pfc. Lynndie England, where there was testimony that intelligence officers were present during prisoner abuse. [Military law expert Eugene FIDELL†- says the law would assume that a commissioned officer would report an offense.] [England’s attorney Rick HERNANDEZ†- says the MPs were given orders by military intelligence.] 
 (Studio: Brian Williams) A new tactic by US forces in the fight against the rebel followers of Muqtada al-Sadr in Iraq noted; scenes shown of US vehicles in Najaf sending warnings over loudspeakers for fighters to disarm.

data.segment_title: Decision 2004 / Bush vs. Kerry / Iraq War
data.segment_description: (Studio: Brian Williams) Report introduced.   (Panama City, Florida: David Gregory) The debate in the presidential election over President Bush’s decision to go to war in Iraq featured; scenes shown of Bush with Senator John McCain in Florida. [Today & yesterday, BUSH – challenges Senator John Kerry to say if he would vote for war.] [Monday, KERRY – questions why Bush rushed to war without a plan to win the peace.] [Public opinion scholar Steven KULL†- notes the danger that Kerry will be seen as having no direction.] [McCAIN – supports Bush’s war decision.]

data.segment_title: Olympic Games / Security / US Women’s Soccer Team
data.segment_description: (Studio: Brian Williams) Figures on security at the Olympic Games in Athens, Greece, cited.   (Crete: Kerry Sanders) How US athletes are being prepared to deal with the threat of terrorism at the Olympics featured; scenes shown of the US women’s soccer team practicing in Crete, where security is tighter than in Athens. [Terrorism analyst Roger CRESSEY†- says US officials are worried that US athletes will be specifically targeted.] [US Olympic Committee spokesman Darryl SEIBEL†- says we’re stressing awareness to our athletes.] [US women’s soccer team captain Julie FOUDY†- relates the reminder to not use the flag to taunt.] [US women’s soccer team goalkeeper Briana SCURRY†- comments on the presence of security forces.] Security for US allies in the war on terror, including Britain & Israel, noted. [Israeli Olympic delegation Efraim ZINGER†- says terrorist activities will not make us afraid.]   (Studio: Brian Williams) More information on msnbc.com noted.

(Studio: Brian Williams) The outrage over the counting of votes in Florida in the 2000 presidential election recalled.

[Licking County, Ohio, Board of Elections Mary Jo LONG†- says we don’t have the problems you saw in Florida in 2000.] [Election law expert Daniel TOKAJI††- says a lot of votes will be lost in Ohio.] [Ohio election official Dana WALCH†- comments on the campaign to train election officials and educate the public on using punch card ballots.]
